title: Implementing an Evidence-based Alcohol Use and Sexual Risk Intervention in Young Adult Homeless Service Settings
official: Implementing an Evidence-based Alcohol Use and Sexual Risk Intervention in Young Adult Homeless Service Settings
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if AWARE-a brief, 4-session group program based on motivational interviewing-reduces alcohol and other drug use and sexual risk behavior among young adults experiencing homelessness (ages 18-25). The study will also learn how well AWARE can be delivered in real-world drop-in center settings and what it would take to keep the program running long-term.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does AWARE reduce the frequency, quantity, and consequences of alcohol use more than services as usual?
* Does AWARE reduce sexual risk behavior (condomless sex with primary and casual partners, number of sexual partners, and alcohol or other drug use during sexual activity)?
* How consistently and well can AWARE be delivered at community drop-in centers?

Researchers will compare AWARE to services as usual at three drop-in centers in Los Angeles and Pittsburgh to see if AWARE works to better.

Participants will:

* Attend up to 4 group sessions of AWARE or continue receiving usual services at their drop-in center
* Complete surveys about their alcohol and drug use, sexual behavior, and health at study enrollment, and 3 and 6 month follow-ups.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* aged 18-25 years
* receiving services at the drop-in center
* plans to stay in the geographic area for the next month
* English speaking

Exclusion Criteria:

* Observed cognitive impairment during enrollment
